cause_quote: The new cleanup-start callback called `recordUpdateRunStep(run.runId, { step: step.name, status: "in_progress", startedAtMs: Date.now() }, { env: run.env })`, so a synchronous write failure escaped before Git could remove the worktree.
user_saw: When update history could not record cleanup, the updater could show a reporting error in place of the original failure and leave the temporary Git worktree behind.
summary: The fix lets temporary Git worktree cleanup proceed when progress writes fail and preserves the original update outcome and recovery classification alongside secondary errors.
reasoning: The parent of #138690 already removed the temporary Git worktree in a finally block and used display-only progress callbacks. #138690 added synchronous ledger writes to those callbacks, and I verified that the existing command runner invoked the start callback before running Git, allowing a write failure to skip removal and replace the initiating error during unwinding. #162098 later awaited progress receipts and continued to propagate ordinary write failures.
